methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $46M total raised proxy.

private.name: Material Evolution
private.rationale: Same sector (Housing & Construction), same stage (Series A)

data.narrative:
Cobod, a Series A housing and construction technology company founded by Henrik Lund-Nielsen, has raised $46M to date. The comparable universe is limited, consisting of one identifiable private peer (Material Evolution) and no public construction-tech comparables, reflecting the nascent stage of frontier technology in this sector.

Valuation analysis relies on a stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($46M) as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $92M. This reflects normalized dilution and value creation expectations between financing rounds in the venture capital sequence.

The triangulated range spans $78M (low) to $106M (high), with $92M as the median point. This narrow $28M band around the median underscores heavy reliance on a single methodology and limited comparable data. Key uncertainties include the applicability of standard venture stage multiples to an emerging construction-tech subsector, traction metrics not captured in available data, and the absence of public market benchmarks or a deeper private comp set to stress-test assumptions. Additional diligence on unit economics, addressable market validation, and technology differentiation would be required to narrow the range or adjust the stage multiplier.
